What comes up in Terrigal

3 conditions, and each one is handled differently

Every site is scoped on the day. The table describes how these jobs generally go in this area. Your block may not match it, which is the reason for looking at it first.

Knockdown on a steep beachside block

The characteristic Terrigal job, where access rather than structure sets the programme.

How it is handled
Smaller plant working for longer, with material moved up the block in stages and loaded at the street.
What does it
Mini and midi excavators, bogie or 10 wheeler tippers.

Holiday era fibro dwelling

Older beach housing that has never been reclad, where the sheeting is the first question.

How it is handled
Condition assessed before disturbance, removed under licence and independently cleared before the structure is touched.
What does it
Licensed asbestos removalists, then a machine once clearance is issued.

Freestanding houses

Single and double storey brick, brick veneer, fibro and timber. The era matters more than the material, because anything built before 1990 carries a hazardous materials assumption until it is tested.

How it is handled
Hazardous materials removed and cleared first, services disconnected in writing, then the structure taken down and the material separated as it falls.
What does it
Excavator with a demolition grapple, sized to the side access rather than to the house. Zero tail swing where the work runs hard against a boundary.

Terrigal

What shapes the work on these blocks

  • Steep coastal blocks Where the fall and the driveway together decide what plant can get on.
  • Narrow beachside streets On which a truck and dog is frequently not an option at all.
  • Holiday era stock beside newer builds Older fibro housing a street away from recent construction, which need very different surveys.
  • High redevelopment pressure Knockdown rebuilds on blocks that were originally modest.

Terrigal is one of the places where the street decides the job. Where a truck and dog cannot stand or turn, the same volume goes out in far more tipper loads, and on the steeper driveways only smaller plant will get on at all.

Terrigal questions

What people ask before we start

Why does the street change the price?
Because it changes the number of loads. A truck and dog carries far more per trip than a tipper, so a street that will not take one turns the same volume into considerably more movements and a longer programme.
Can you work on a block with a steep driveway?
Usually, with smaller plant working for longer. The route in and the route out for material are both settled at the site visit before a price is given.
Why is asbestos such a feature of Central Coast work?
Because a great deal of the older housing is pre 1990 fibro, much of it holiday era stock that was never replaced. Identification sits at the front of most jobs here for that reason.
How many contractors am I dealing with if there is asbestos on site?
One. Max holds demolition licence AD214737, licensed asbestos removalists carry out the removal, and an independent licensed assessor does the air monitoring and clearance. Sequencing the three of them is our job, not yours.
